**Issue #3727 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3727: Patch: daily games, a move every 1, 3, 7 or 14 days, by challenge or the daily queue, with an email or a push when it's your move
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

A new way to play online, like a daily (correspondence) game on chess.com or Lichess. Each player has days, not seconds, to make a move, so one game lasts days or weeks. A player keeps several daily games going at once, logs in once a day or every few days, plays their move in each game that is waiting on them, and gets an email or a push notification when a game is waiting.

It is also how crossplay will work once there is a Roblox client (#2898). A Roblox game's servers and ours can't hold a live match together, but a daily game needs nothing live: each move is one HTTPS request. Later, a Roblox server can play its players' daily games through the same API; that follow-up is its own issue in the tracker. This changes #2898's constraint "No cross-platform play". The owner decided on 2026-11-11 that crossplay happens through daily games.

Nothing about daily games exists yet. A search for daily, correspondence, async and time control across the crates, the spec and the apps finds nothing. The server assumes every match is live and in memory ("Under the hood" below).

### How it plays

**Starting a game.** There are two ways, and each picks a mode, a deck and a time per move:

- **Challenge a player.** Pick a friend, a mode, a deck and a time per move. A live challenge goes only to a friend who is online and in no match, and it lapses after `CHALLENGE_TTL_MS` (2 minutes, §9.5). A daily challenge also goes to a friend who is offline or in a game. It waits up to `DAILY_CHALLENGE_TTL_DAYS` (say 7) for the friend to accept with a deck of their own or decline. The challenger can cancel it.
- **The daily queue.** Pick a mode, a deck and a time per move. The server pairs you with the next player who queued for the same mode and the same time per move. While daily games are unranked this needs no rating window. A daily game is never paired with a ladder bot: R1452's bot fallback is for the live queue only. A seek waits up to `DAILY_SEEK_TTL_DAYS` and can be cancelled.

**Modes.** Only the two modes that are a single game:

- **Best of 1**, with one saved deck.
- **All Random**, which deals both players a deck (R258), with the "More cards from" lean (R1372, R924000).

Conquest's trio series is out of the first cut.

**Time per move:** 1 day, 3 days, 1 week or 2 weeks. The four choices are one list in `crates/shared/src/config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9). The clock is per move, as on chess.com: each time the move passes to a player, that player gets the full time again. Unused time does not carry over.

**What a move is.** A player has the move from the moment the game waits on them until it waits on the other player:

- **Their turn.** From the start of the turn until End turn. Every action in between is sent to the server and applied at once, as in a live match: playing a card, attacking, answering their own prompt. Leaving mid-turn leaves the turn where it is, and the clock keeps running.
- **A prompt for the other player.** A prompt for the other player in the middle of a turn hands the move to them with a fresh full window, and back once they answer. An example is a trap that fires on its owner's opponent's turn; in a live match this is R79's 30-second prompt clock.
- **The mulligan.** Both players have the move at once, each with their own window. The first turn starts once both have answered.

**When the time runs out**, the player who had the move loses, as `disconnectExpired` loses a live game. In a live match R79's `timeout` only answers for the player and ends the turn. In a daily game that would let an absent player drag a game out to the turn cap. This is a new ruling.

**The rest of a live game still holds:**

- A player can concede at any time, from the board or from the games list.
- A draw offer stands until the other player's next move.
- The engine's turn cap (`TURN_CAP_PLAYER_TURNS`) ends a game that runs long.
- The 120-minute ceiling (`MATCH_CEILING_MINUTES`) does not apply.
- KY's Competition (Meditative+ #20) has a 60-second window that its host keeps (R1563006). A daily game can't keep it, so this needs a ruling. Suggested: the move's own deadline is the window.

**A card patch mid-game.** A daily game can outlive a card patch. It folds under the catalog version it started on for its whole life; the replay fold already folds under older shipped catalogs (R767000). Its board says when it is played on an older version.

**Many games at once.** A player may hold up to `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` (say 20) daily games, open seeks and open challenges together, and play a live game on top of them. A daily game holds no seat in the seat ledger (`crates/server/src/seats.rs`): R1523000's one game per profile is for live games. This is a ruling.

**After the game.** The result panel offers a rematch as a new daily challenge with the same settings. Daily games are unranked in this first cut. They count for quests, rewards and statistics as a friend's room game does (§9.11, §14.8).

**Blocking** a player cancels the open daily challenges between you, as R1689000 does for live challenges. Suggested: a daily game already running goes on. The planner checks this against §9.8.

### Telling a player it's their move

- **In the client.** The Play button and the Daily screen carry a badge with the number of games waiting on you. The tab title reads "Your move (3)", as `routes/match.tsx:336` already does for a live turn. The `/ws/social` socket's `social` frame (`crates/server/src/social/live.rs`) carries the count, so an open tab updates without polling.
- **Email.**
  - It is sent when a game starts waiting on you, and once more `DAILY_REMINDER_HOURS` (say 12) before a deadline if you still haven't moved.
  - An account gets at most one email every `DAILY_EMAIL_MIN_GAP_HOURS` (say 6). Each email lists every game waiting, each with a link straight to its board.
  - A setting turns these emails off. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe link and the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers.
  - Mail goes through Resend's API, which the server already calls for operator alerts (`crates/server/src/alerts.rs`), under a new server-only key. With the key unset, the server sends nothing.
  - Accounts with no email, such as those signed in with Roblox (R3147000), get none.
- **Push.**
  - Web push goes to every device the player turned it on for. It needs a service worker, the Push API and a VAPID key pair: the public key is a public variable (`docs/architecture.md` §8.1), the private key server-only (§8.2).
  - On an iPad or iPhone, Safari delivers web push only to a site added to the Home Screen (iPadOS and iOS 16.4 and later). So the client gets a web app manifest and icons (`apps/web/public/`), and the Daily screen explains Add to Home Screen there.
  - When the push service answers 404 or 410 for a subscription, the server deletes it. Signing out deletes the device's subscription.
- **What to send is a pure decision.** Which emails and pushes go out is decided in `crates/shared`, from the games waiting, what was last sent and the player's settings (CLAUDE.md rule 4). The server only does the sending.
- **The Privacy Policy** (`routes/privacy.tsx`) names what this keeps: the notification settings and the push subscriptions.

### Under the hood

- **Nothing stays in memory between moves.**
  - Today a live match is an actor held in memory (`crates/server/src/actor/`), and the server sleeps after 5 minutes with no request (`SLEEP_AFTER` in `apps/edge/src/index.ts`).
  - A daily game is its `matches` row, its `match_actions` log and a `match_checkpoints` row. Each move loads the game, applies the action through the engine, appends it, and writes the next deadline and who has the move.
  - So the game survives the server sleeping, restarting and being deployed.
- **A migration** (the next number after `0087`) adds:
  - the time control, the deadline and who has the move;
  - daily challenges and seeks;
  - the notification settings and the push subscriptions.

  Its RLS follows `docs/architecture.md` §3.2 and is checked by `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`. The store change goes in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`. The 90-day log retention (`MATCH_ACTION_RETENTION_DAYS`) counts from a game's end and never purges a running game.
- **Deadlines while nobody is online.** Something has to end expired games and send the emails while the server sleeps.
  - Add a Worker cron every `DAILY_SWEEP_MINUTES` (hourly is enough) that wakes the server's sweep. The daily `23 14 * * *` wake-up in `wrangler.jsonc` stays (CLAUDE.md rule 13).
  - Any read of a game past its deadline also applies the loss right then, so no screen shows a game past its time between sweeps.
- **The clock is pure.** The daily clock goes in the host machine (`crates/shared/src/host/`: `clock.rs`, `timer.rs`), beside the live clock. It decides who has the move, the deadline, and what an expiry becomes.
- **The API is plain HTTPS, so crossplay can use it.** Its routes:
  - list my daily games, challenges and seeks;
  - challenge, accept, decline and cancel;
  - seek and cancel a seek;
  - read a game: the seat's `view_for`, its legal actions, the deadline, who has the move and its catalog version;
  - send an action along with the sequence number it follows, so a retried request applies once and a stale one is refused.

  Playing a daily game needs no socket, no in-browser engine and no cookie. The web may still use the social socket for its badges. Each route is documented in `crates/server/README.md`, and the boundary in `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md`.

### The web

- **A Daily screen**, `/daily`, reached from Play. A new route touches `net/navigate.ts`'s `paths`, `routes/chunks.tsx`, `net/head.ts`, `public/_redirects`, `isBoardPath` and `routes/commandEntries.ts`.
  - It lists, in order: Your move (the least time left first), Their move, challenges in and out, seeks, and recently finished games.
  - Each game is one row: the opponent's name and portrait, the mode, the turn number, both heroes' life, and "Your move · 1d 4h left". The time turns an urgent colour under `DAILY_URGENT_HOURS`.
- **The board** is the ordinary one (`Game.tsx`):
  - The clock pill shows days and hours for whoever has the move.
  - End turn says that it sends the move.
  - Once the move is sent, a **Next game** button opens the next game waiting on you, as chess.com and Lichess do. Clearing ten games takes ten turns, not ten trips back to a list.
- **A New daily game dialog**: Challenge a friend (any friend, online or not) or Find an opponent; then the mode, the deck, and the time per move as a segmented control of the four choices.
- **The friends panel's Challenge** offers Live (an online friend, as now) or Daily (any friend).
- **A notifications setting**: email on or off, and push on this device.
- **Built on what exists.** It uses the existing components (`buttons.css`'s roles, the shared Dialog, Tabs and segmented toggle from #3219–#3222) and tokens. It is laid out for desktop and iPad first and is passable on a phone. The tracker's app-shell issue fits it into the new navigation later.

### Out of scope

These are follow-ups, kept in the tracker:

- ranked daily games and a daily ladder;
- Conquest and Duos daily games;
- vacation days and planned moves;
- watching a friend's daily game;
- a Roblox server playing through the API (the tracker's crossplay issue).

### Acceptance

- **Spec.** §9.5 gains a daily-games subsection, or a new §9.13 holds it, with the rules above. Each decision the spec didn't make gets a ruling note proven by a test named after it (CLAUDE.md rule 3):
  - a timeout loses;
  - a prompt hands over the move with a fresh window;
  - the mulligan;
  - KY's Competition;
  - a daily game holds no seat;
  - the catalog version.

  `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- **`crates/shared` tests** for the daily clock and the notification decision: who has the move after each kind of action, the deadline, an expiry, the reminder, and the gap between emails.
- **Server tests:**
  - A daily game is played to its end across a server restart, rebuilt from the store between moves.
  - A move after its deadline is refused, and the game is lost on time, whether the sweep finds it or a read does.
  - The same action sent twice applies once.
  - A game started on a catalog version plays on that version after a fixture patch ships, and its replay hashes.
  - A player with `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` daily games still queues for and plays a live game, and is refused one daily game more.
  - A daily challenge to an offline friend opens, and one to a stranger is refused.
  - A block cancels the open daily challenges between the two players.
  - With a fake mailer, the sweep sends one email per account, none to an account with the setting off, and none to an account with no email.
  - A push subscription answered 410 is deleted.
- **The store contract and the SQL suite** cover the new tables and their RLS.
- **Web tests:**
  - unit tests for the list's order, the time-left wording and the badge;
  - a Cypress spec in which two players start a daily game by challenge, each moves, and "Your move" passes between them;
  - a second spec in which the server's clock is set past a deadline and the game shows as lost on time.
- **Screenshots** in the pull request of the Daily screen and a daily board at 1440×900, iPad landscape 1180×820, iPad portrait 820×1180, and phone 390×844.
- **Every required check is green** (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

### Blocked by, part of

Part of #3726.

### For the builder

- **Rulings** take this issue's block (`docs/issues-and-patches.md`, Ruling numbers).
- **Secrets.** A person adds the two secrets the code reads: the Resend key for player mail and the VAPID key pair (`infra/` or the Worker's secrets, `docs/deploy-cloudflare.md`). Everything else is code. With them unset, the server sends no email or push, and every test runs on fakes.
- **Size.** This is large. If a single build is too much, it splits well along these lines: the spec and the pure clock; the store and the API; the sweep and notifications; the web.
```
